title: ID0414780-DC/Si-D/TR-[MP / S3 170003330] PowerConverters-Missing Converters in DC4,3
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
Missing Converters in DC4,3
Solution:
Possible KF214 problem

additional_info.subject: ID0414780-DC/Si-D/TR-[MP / S3 170003330] PowerConverters-Missing Converters in DC4,3 CRM:00315002469
additional_info.body:
Dear Emre-abi,
Thank you for reaching
out
to eMobility Support. My name is
Francisco
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
MP / S3 170003330
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
3p0jka
Problem Description
: DC3 and DC4 converter groups are missing
Troubleshooting
:
Here is how the fast shutdown works with (and for) the dispenser:
The StateMonitor of the main charger is constantly sending 12V to the dispenser (since we have a dispenser the QAs are not necessary for operation).
When the StateMonitor from the dispenser has the 12V, he will send another 12V back to the main charger, via FA10 (DC4) and via FA11 (DC3), when requested to do the Fast shutdown.
Here the problems seems that the 12V coming from the output of the dispenser's StateMonitor is constantly ON. Why do I say this? Because if you take a look at the error flags, we can see that the converters only have the CAN communication established. When you have F=0 it means that the converter is not “powered on”, which is a consequence of having the 12V in the Fast shutdown line.
One thing to note is that the dispenser schematic that it's on SCB is incorrect.
What we need to measure is the following:
If we have 12V at the SuO of both sides. If we have 12V then please replace the KF214 (the SuC is the input from main charger).
If we don't have 12V at the output then that means that something is mis-wired in the FA10/FA11.
For future reference, your case number is
0414780
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Francisco de Matos Joaquim
